title: Ops Snaplet Factory for Safe Shortflows
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a lightweight 'snaplet factory' that converts field support runbook steps into audited, parameterized shortflows (aka snaplets) that can be composed into larger repair sequences. Goals: (1) reduce time-to-remediate for common incidents by providing pre-validated, idempotent micro-actions; (2) ensure every snaplet has automatic telemetry and a safety gate (dry-run + approval meta) so novice on-call can execute without exposing privileged long-lived credentials; (3) provide a developer ergonomics surface (CLI + small UI) for authoring and testing snaplets locally before publishing to the ops catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Authoring CLI: implement 'ri snaplet create|test|publish' with flags for inputs, required RBAC scope, and dry-run mode
Audit metadata: each published snaplet includes immutable version, who-published, k/v of expected side effects, and Concourse-style provenance link
Dry-run harness: executing a snaplet with --dry-run must not modify production resources and produce a readable plan output
Safety policy: snaplets touching IAM, DB schema, or billing-tier changes require staged approval and explicit reviewer recorded in audit
Telemetry: executions emit structured telemetry to ops.metrics (snaplet.id, snapshot_hash, result:OK/FAIL, duration_ms, actor)
implementation_notes: Reuse existing runbook parser from ops-playflow to extract step metadata and idempotency hints

Implement snaplet runtime as a thin wrapper that validates inputs, checks cached assertions (KV cache), then invokes targeted admin adapters (kubectl, sql-runner, billing-api) behind service-account glue
Store published snaplets in 'ops-snaplet-catalog' S3 bucket with metadata index and signed manifest
Design CLI to produce a deterministic hash of the snaplet spec so deployments can reference versions (snaplet:v1@sha256:...)
Plan to gate IAM-affecting snaplets behind 'enterprise-privileged' playbook which requires at least two approvers
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal dev team only; publish 10 initial snaplets (kube restart, rotate cache key, collect logs) and run smoke tests
Phase 1 (pilot): SRE oncall uses factory for non-privileged shortflows; gather execution telemetry and error modes for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (wider): open catalog to firstline support with training doc and ~20 curated snaplets; require approval gating for high-risk actions
Phase 3 (optimize): add UI listing and per-snaplet cost/latency breakdown; integrate with autodoc generator

comments: Priya Nair: Important to keep snaplets composable and small (prefer <8 lines of side-effecting commands). Avoid building monolithic 'fixers'.
Aisha Malik (SRE): We should add an option to attach a preflight test that runs against a canary namespace before allowing publish.
Alex Kim (Support): For pilot, please include examples for routine DB connection reset and feature-flag toggles — those are common firstline tasks.
Marco Alvarez: Noted — adding --preflight-hook flag and a template for connection-reset snaplet.
test_plan: Unit: CLI arg parsing + deterministic hash generation
Integration: runtime shim against staging adapters with --dry-run and full-exec modes
Safety: simulate privileged snaplet attempt and verify approval gate blocks publish
E2E: publish a snaplet in staging, execute via web UI and CLI, assert telemetry and audit log entries appear
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Snaplets accidentally expose credentials. Mitigation: enforce service-account scoping and disallow embedding secrets in snaplet specs; fail publish on secret patterns.
Risk: Over-proliferation of poorly-tested snaplets. Mitigation: require minimum test coverage and a review label for first publish; autopromote after N successful executions.
Risk: High-risk actions executed by inexperienced users. Mitigation: approval gating and UI warnings; require 2-step approval for IAM/billing/db-schema actions.
